transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess… my eating’s been kind of all over the place lately. Some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m up after everyone’s gone to bed, just standing in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets. It’s been bothering me.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss recently, or do you feel that you're currently underweight?

I don’t know about underweight… I haven’t really been tracking it. It’s more that my appetite is just strange lately. Some days I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen late eating crackers or sweets.
Do you ever find yourself eating a large amount of food in a short period of time, like a few hours or less, and feel like you can’t stop or control how much you’re eating?

Sometimes, I guess. It’s not like a huge planned thing… more that I’ll barely eat dinner, and then later, after everyone’s asleep, I’m standing there eating crackers or sweets. It feels kind of hard to pull myself away once I start.
Do these eating habits bother you or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yeah… it bothers me. That’s kind of why I came in. It’s just been all over the place—some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m up after everyone’s asleep eating crackers or sweets in the kitchen. It makes me feel… not great about myself.
Have you ever tried to make up for overeating by doing things like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising more than usual?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t made myself throw up or anything like that. I don’t really use laxatives. And exercise… not really more than usual.
Do you feel that your eating behaviors are related to concerns about your weight or shape, or do you worry about gaining weight?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I mean, I don’t like feeling bad about myself after, but I’m not sure it’s about my weight exactly.
Do you find yourself eating this way more when you're feeling stressed, sad, or upset?

Maybe… yeah. I mean, I haven’t tracked it exactly. It’s just what finally made me come in—my eating’s been really all over the place. Some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep, eating crackers or sweets.
Do you find that these nighttime eating episodes happen more often when you're feeling emotionally down, stressed, or upset?

Yeah… maybe. I don’t know if it’s always when I’m upset, but that’s sort of what made me come in. My eating’s been all over the place—some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen late, eating crackers or sweets after everyone’s asleep.
Do these nighttime eating episodes usually happen after you’ve already gone to sleep and then woke up?

Not usually after I’ve been asleep, no. It’s more like… everyone’s gone to bed and I’m still up, and I end up in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets. My eating’s just been kind of all over the place.
Have your eating behaviors caused you problems in your relationships, work, or other important areas of your life?

Yeah… a bit. I’ve fallen behind on some facilitator training and the private blog stuff I was trying to keep up with. It’s like my projects and even explaining what I’m doing got harder to organize.

And at home… there’s been tension, so keeping normal routines with my husband has been harder. I don’t really like talking about that, but yeah, it’s affected things.
When you're eating in the kitchen at night, do you feel like you can't control how much you're eating or that you can't stop once you start?

A little, maybe. It’s not like I plan to eat a lot, but once I’m standing there with the crackers or sweets, I kind of just keep going. My eating’s been really uneven lately… that’s part of why I came in.
Do the nighttime eating episodes themselves cause you distress or affect your ability to function during the day, like making it harder to focus or get things done?

Yeah… I think it does, some. I’ve fallen behind on my facilitator training and the blog work I was trying to do. It’s just harder to organize my projects, or even explain what I’m trying to do.

And at home it’s… tense, so keeping normal routines with my husband has been harder. I don’t really want to get into all of that, but yes, it affects things.
When you’re eating in the kitchen at night, do you feel like you’re not in control of your eating, like you can’t stop once you start?

Yeah… sometimes. I mean, what really made me come in is my eating’s just been all over the place. Some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep, eating crackers or sweets, and it’s harder to stop than I expect.
Do you feel a lot of distress or find it hard to function in important parts of your life specifically because of the episodes where you eat a lot at night?

I guess… yes, somewhat. It’s not only the eating, but that’s what finally pushed me to come in. My eating’s been all over the place—some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m just standing in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets after everyone’s gone to bed. It bothers me.
Do you usually start eating in the kitchen after you’ve already fallen asleep and then woke up, or are you still awake when these episodes start?
I’m usually still awake, I think. It’s after everyone’s gone to bed, and I’m just… in the kitchen, eating crackers or sweets. It’s not like I remember waking up already eating.
How often do these nighttime eating episodes happen? Do they occur most nights, or several times a week?

It’s kind of uneven. Some weeks I barely eat dinner at all, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep, eating crackers or sweets. I don’t know if I’d say most nights… just off and on.
Would you say that your nighttime eating episodes happen at least three times a week on average?

I’m not sure it’s three times a week on average. It’s more uneven than that… some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m up after everyone’s gone to bed eating crackers or sweets. That’s the part that’s been bothering me.
Would you say that your nighttime eating episodes happen at least once a week on average?

Probably at least once a week, yeah. It’s not every night, but… my eating’s been all over the place lately. Some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I end up in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep, eating crackers or sweets.
